about.title: Coalinga Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Coalinga is a small city, and losing someone here often means the loss is felt across a whole circle of family and neighbors. While recent public crash records show no traffic deaths counted in the latest reporting year, collisions still occur on corridors like Rt 33, Forest Avenue, E Polk Street, and E Elm Avenue, and fatal outcomes can happen even when yearly counts are low. If a crash, a workplace incident, or another party's negligence has taken a family member, California law gives certain surviving spouses, domestic partners, children, or dependents the right to bring a wrongful death claim. This is a civil case, entirely separate from any criminal charges that may or may not be filed. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we simply connect Fresno County families with an independent attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what losses may be recoverable, so you can focus on your family while someone else handles the legal groundwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Coalinga Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who can file — typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with certain dependents or heirs eligible afterward. An attorney can help sort out who has standing before time or opportunity is lost.

items.title: The Clock Is Short
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks considerably if a government entity is involved. Getting connected early preserves options.

items.title: No Cost Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront fee and no fee at all unless money is recovered on your behalf. That's true whether the case settles or requires more time to resolve.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives first priority to a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may qualify to bring the claim. An independent attorney can look at your specific family situation and explain who has standing.

items.question: Coalinga's crash data shows zero traffic deaths in the most recent year — does that mean wrongful death claims are rare here?
items.answer: Public crash counts can vary year to year, and a single fatal incident on a road like Rt 33 or E Elm Avenue can still happen even when a prior year's total was low. Wrongful death claims also aren't limited to traffic crashes — they can arise from workplace accidents, defective products, or other negligence. If you've lost a loved one, it's worth having a conversation regardless of what the yearly averages show.

items.question: How long do we have to bring a wrongful death claim after losing a family member?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives two years from the date of death to file. That deadline is often much shorter if a government agency or employee was involved in causing the death. Because these timelines are strict, reaching out sooner rather than later helps preserve your options.
